members.name: cross_listed_arb_v1
members.universe: Liquid mid-cap stocks listed on both NSE and BSE (e.g., VOLTAS, GODREJCP, MPHASIS)
members.thesis: Stocks listed on both NSE and BSE can exhibit transient price divergences of 2-10 bps due to differential order flow, varying market microstructure (NSE has higher HFT participation), and latency differences between exchange matching engines. While professional arbitrageurs keep the spread tight on
entry_long: price_diff_bps > 5 (NSE trading higher than BSE by >5bps)
entry_short: price_diff_bps < -5 (BSE trading higher than NSE by >5bps)
members.exit_stop: price_diff_bps exceeds 15bps against position OR loss > 0.2%
filters: none (arb works in all VIX regimes)
best windows: 09:20-10:00 and 14:30-15:25 (open/close have more BSE dislocations)
BSE 1-min volume must be > 500 shares (minimum for executable arb)
combined bid-ask spread across both exchanges < 8bps
weaknesses: BSE liquidity for mid-caps is extremely thin; large orders can move the BSE price against you, and fills may be partial or delayed
Zerodha doesn't support true simultaneous cross-exchange execution; the latency between placing NSE and BSE orders creates leg risk
Settlement and clearing across two exchanges adds operational complexity; T+1 settlement mismatches can occur
members.prior_art: Gagnon & Karolyi (2010) cross-listing price parity; adapted for NSE-BSE dual listing. Similar to Subrahmanyam (1994) on multi-market microstructure.

members.name: dual_listing_spread_v1
members.thesis: Stocks listed on both NSE and BSE occasionally show price discrepancies of 5-15 bps due to fragmented liquidity and different order flow composition on each exchange. These spreads mean-revert within minutes because arbitrageurs eventually close the gap. However, the Zerodha cost structure makes thi
entry_long: abs(spread_bps) > 8 (minimum 8 bps spread to cover costs)
members.exit_stop: spread_zscore reaches ±3.5 or 15 bps absolute loss on spread
filters: no trades first 15 min (both exchanges stabilizing)
BSE volume must be > 50% of NSE volume for that bar (sufficient BSE liquidity)
abs(spread_bps) > 8 bps minimum (must exceed round-trip costs)
weaknesses: BSE liquidity is very thin for most stocks — execution risk is the primary concern
Four-leg cost (buy+sell on two exchanges) is extremely high; gross spread must be > 20 bps to profit
Zerodha's BSE execution may not be fast enough — latency kills this strategy
members.prior_art: Cross-exchange arbitrage — one of the oldest arbitrage strategies in any market
